title: Izanagi and Izanami
subtitle: A creation retelling and its source frame

learningObjectives.text: How do Izanagi and Izanami create the islands?
What goes wrong at their wedding?

main.work: Old-World Japan: The creation episode in Old-World Japan
main.author: Frank Rinder
main.locator: The creation episode in Old-World Japan; local text normalized characters 6915-7386
main.excerpt: Now Izanagi and Izanami wandered on the Floating Bridge of Heaven. This bridge spanned the gulf between heaven and the unformed world; it was upheld in the air, and it stood secure. The God of the Air spoke to the Goddess of the Clouds: "There must needs be a kingdom beneath us, let us visit it." When he had so said, he plunged his jewelled spear into the seething mass below. The drops that fell from the point of the spear congealed and became the island of Onogoro.
main.note: Rinder's modern retelling, not a direct Kojiki translation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The spear and the brine
narrativeBlocks.body: The elder gods send Izanagi and Izanami down from the Floating Bridge of Heaven. They thrust the jeweled spear into the ocean brine and lift it — and the drops falling from its point become Onogoro, the first island.

narrativeBlocks.title: The wedding around the pillar
narrativeBlocks.body: On Onogoro they build the heavenly pillar and marry by circling it — but Izanami greets her husband first, a breach of order. Their firstborn is the deformed Hiruko, the leech-child, set adrift in a boat of reeds.

narrativeBlocks.title: A second rite, a better birth
narrativeBlocks.body: They redo the wedding properly — the man speaking first — and this time the union succeeds: from their embrace are born the islands of Japan itself, then the kami of wind, trees, mountains, and seas.

narrativeBlocks.title: The birth that burns
narrativeBlocks.body: Then Izanami bears the fire god, and it kills her. The creation that began with drops of brine ends at death's door — and Izanagi's grief will take him into the underworld later this week.

narrativeBlocks.title: Gods who live close
narrativeBlocks.body: In Shinto, the kami are not remote: the land itself is born of gods, and gods marry, err, grieve, and die. That closeness shapes every story this week.

quiz.prompt: What do the drops from the jeweled spear become?

choices.text: Onogoro — the first island, where Izanagi and Izanami begin creation

quiz.explanation: The spear-drops make Onogoro — the platform for everything after.

quiz.prompt: Why is the first child, Hiruko, deformed?

choices.text: Because Izanami spoke first at the pillar wedding — a breach of the rite's order
The fire god burned him in the womb
He was born in the underworld

quiz.explanation: The flawed rite produces the flawed child — ritual order matters.
